name: Retained Medullary Cord

criteria.description: Presence of a nonfunctional medullary cord extending beyond the conus medullaris on MRI
Clinical signs of tethered cord syndrome such as lower limb neurological deficits or bladder dysfunction
Intraoperative identification of a fibrous medullary cord without functional neural tissue
Exclusion of other spinal dysraphism such as lipomyelomeningocele or thickened filum terminale

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a nonfunctional medullary cord on imaging and clinical signs of tethered cord syndrome confirmed intraoperatively
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires correlation of imaging, clinical presentation, and surgical findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nonfunctional medullary cord extending beyond conus medullaris
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on MRI and confirmed intraoperatively
searchTerms: abnormal spinal cord extension beyond normal end
spinal cord tissue extending too far
extra spinal cord tissue below conus medullaris

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome with neurological deficits
searchTerms: spinal cord tethering causing nerve problems
tight spinal cord with neurological symptoms
spinal cord stuck causing weakness or numbness

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata over the lumbosacral region
searchTerms: birthmarks or skin changes on lumbosacral area
skin abnormalities on lower spine region
abnormal sensations in feet and legs

rare.symptomName: Neurogenic bladder with recurrent urinary tract infections
searchTerms: bladder nerve problems with repeated urinary infections
poor bladder control with frequent UTIs
increased muscle tone in lower limbs

imaging: MRI showing a nonfunctional medullary cord extending beyond the conus medullaris
other: Intraoperative confirmation of fibrous medullary cord without functional neural tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Tethered cord syndrome may be caused by thickened filum terminale or lipomyelomeningocele rather than retained medullary cord
Presence of functional neural tissue in tethered cord syndrome unlike nonfunctional cord in RMC
Presence of lipomatous mass on imaging
Different surgical approach and pathology compared to retained medullary cord

redFlags: New onset bladder or bowel dysfunction
references: Kawabata S, et al. Retained medullary cord: a newly recognized entity of closed spinal dysraphism. Neurosurgery. 2016.
